Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL PROFILE
Data Scientist with experience building and evaluating forecasting, churn-modelling and experimentation solutions using Python, SQL and cloud data tools. Work includes feature engineering, scheduled model workflows, batch scoring and measurable business outcomes. Transitioning toward machine learning engineering, with recent experience adding pytest unit tests to forecasting feature code and building a Dockerfile for a Streamlit application.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python, SQL, R, pandas, scikit-learn
Machine learning and statistics: LightGBM, XGBoost, SHAP, statsmodels, feature engineering, forecasting, churn modelling, experimentation, Bayesian hierarchical modelling
Platforms and tools: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker, dbt, dbt Cloud scheduler, Streamlit, Docker, pytest, R Markdown
Learning project: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox | 2022–Present
- Built a weekly recipe-demand forecasting workflow using LightGBM, with calendar, price and menu-position features to forecast orders by recipe and region six weeks ahead.
- Scheduled the forecasting notebook in Vertex AI Workbench to write results to BigQuery for operational use in Looker. Improved WAPE from 23% to 14%; estimated food-waste reduction was 9%.
- Developed a weekly XGBoost churn-scoring workflow in BigQuery, using dbt, and supported retention targeting of top-decile customers. In a 10% holdout validation, churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group.
- Built a Streamlit calculator for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests, used by approximately 25 people in product and growth. Wrote its Dockerfile; the data platform team handled deployment to Cloud Run.
- Began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.
- Delivered the internal training session “Stats for PMs” three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | 2020–2022
- Segmented customers and analysed tariffs using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

EDUCATION
MSc Statistics | [UNIVERSITY] | [YEAR]
- Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models

ADDITIONAL PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | Personal | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep-learning course; achieved approximately 80% accuracy.
- Learning project using PyTorch, torchvision and Google Colab.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally structured and strongly evidence-based. It uses measurable outcomes effectively, including the WAPE improvement from 23% to 14%, estimated 9% food-waste reduction, 2.1-percentage-point churn reduction and adoption by approximately 25 users. The experience bullets explain the modelling work, workflow scheduling and business use rather than listing tools without context. The profile also responsibly describes the transition toward machine learning engineering and does not overclaim API deployment or platform ownership. The main content weaknesses are the unresolved placeholders ([EMAIL], [PHONE], [LINKEDIN], [UNIVERSITY], [YEAR]) and limited detail about software-engineering practices, monitoring, versioning and data pipelines relevant to this particular role. These are partly genuine experience gaps rather than wording problems.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly parseable: it uses standard section headings, chronological experience, simple bullets and no tables, graphics or unusual formatting. Relevant keywords such as Python, SQL, feature engineering, forecasting, batch scoring, Docker, pytest, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Streamlit and Cloud Run are present. AI screening probability for this specific vacancy is moderate to low because the document does not contain the central target terms chat assistants, RAG, language models, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow or Airflow; the candidate's source material also does not support adding most of them. The CV could make supported orchestration and pipeline terminology more explicit, particularly scheduled workflows, dbt Cloud scheduler, BigQuery batch scoring and writing model outputs to BigQuery. The placeholders for contact and education details could also interfere with recruiter confidence, even though they should parse correctly.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV demonstrates relevant foundations for a developing machine learning engineer: Python, feature engineering, model evaluation, scheduled ML workflows, batch scoring, GCP-based tools, Docker, pytest and business-facing delivery. It aligns particularly well with feature engineering, cloud exposure, experimentation and data-processing workflows. It does not establish the role's core must-haves of four years as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production, AI products such as chat assistants or RAG, or production software engineering covering model serving, monitoring and data versioning. The candidate's own notes confirm that forecasting is a scheduled notebook, churn is SQL batch scoring, the candidate has not independently deployed a model as an API, and there is no Kubernetes, MLflow or Airflow experience. These are genuine job-alignment gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting. The MSc Statistics is relevant quantitative education, although it is not an exact machine learning, computer science or engineering degree. The document shows a credible transition profile, but it is not yet a strong match for a role requiring an experienced production MLE focused on customer-support AI.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the header, replace [EMAIL], [PHONE] and [LINKEDIN] with the candidate's actual professional contact details. Do not leave bracketed placeholders in the submitted CV.
2. In the Education section, replace [UNIVERSITY] and [YEAR] with the actual institution and graduation year. Keep the factual degree title as “MSc Statistics” and do not relabel it as machine learning or computer science.
3. In the Professional Profile, make the supported production scope more explicit without implying API deployment. For example, change the second sentence to: “Experience includes feature engineering, scheduled model workflows, BigQuery batch scoring, model-output pipelines and measurable business outcomes.” Retain the statement about transitioning toward machine learning engineering because it accurately sets expectations.
4. In the Technical Skills section, change “Platforms and tools: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker, dbt, dbt Cloud scheduler, Streamlit, Docker, pytest, R Markdown” to “Cloud, orchestration and tools: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, scheduled notebooks, dbt, dbt Cloud scheduler, Looker, Streamlit, Docker, pytest, R Markdown.” This surfaces the orchestration experience already documented without adding Airflow, MLflow or Kubernetes.
5. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the forecasting bullet to make the data workflow and orchestration clearer: “Built and scheduled a weekly LightGBM forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench, using calendar, price and menu-position features; wrote six-week-ahead recipe-and-region forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker.” Keep the existing metrics in the following bullet.
6. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the churn bullet to explicitly use supported pipeline language: “Developed a weekly XGBoost churn batch-scoring workflow in BigQuery, orchestrated with dbt, and supported retention targeting of top-decile customers.” Do not describe this as model serving or real-time inference.
7. In the Thistlebox experience section, preserve the qualification in the Streamlit bullet but make ownership boundaries immediately clear: “Built and containerised a Streamlit calculator for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests; wrote the Dockerfile, while the data platform team deployed it to Cloud Run.” This is more concise and avoids implying that the candidate operated the deployment platform.

MINOR:
8. In the “Learning project” skills line, change the label to “Course project: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab” so ATS and recruiters do not interpret this as professional deep-learning production experience.
9. In the Additional Project section, change “achieved approximately 80% accuracy” to “achieved approximately 80% accuracy on the course project’s public food-images dataset” if that accurately reflects the evaluation setup; otherwise retain the current wording. This keeps the result appropriately scoped.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured and professional CV with strong quantified evidence. The Thistlebox experience is particularly effective: it explains the modelling work, delivery workflow, technologies, and outcomes such as WAPE improving from 23% to 14%, estimated food-waste reduction of 9%, and a 2.1 percentage-point reduction in churn. The document is also appropriately honest about the candidate's transition toward machine learning engineering and the limited deployment ownership. The main content limitation is that the profile and skills section do not make the strongest possible connection between the candidate's existing work and production-oriented ML engineering concepts such as GCP, orchestration, batch serving, testing, and data pipelines.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly headings, standard text formatting, readable bullets, and conventional chronological structure. Relevant keywords are present, including Python, SQL, feature engineering, forecasting, batch scoring, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Docker, pytest, Streamlit, LightGBM, and XGBoost. However, strict ATS screening for this role is likely to be moderate-to-low because the document does not contain several high-priority terms from the advertisement: AI assistants, RAG, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, or LLM observability. These are genuine experience gaps rather than keywords that should be added without evidence. The cloud experience would parse more reliably if explicitly grouped under 'GCP' rather than listed only as BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a credible match for the data science and applied ML portions of the role. It shows Python, feature engineering, model evaluation, scheduled workflows, batch scoring, GCP technologies, experimentation, data transformation with dbt, automated testing, and operational use of model outputs. It also demonstrates measurable business impact and experience collaborating with product, growth, operations, and a data platform team. The candidate's material does not show four years as a machine learning engineer, AI assistants or RAG, model serving ownership, monitoring, data versioning, or the named MLOps tools requested. The MSc Statistics is relevant quantitative education but is not explicitly a degree in machine learning, computer science, or engineering. These gaps substantially reduce alignment with this specific Customer Support AI MLE role, although the CV presents the existing experience truthfully and could suit a junior or transitioning MLE role more closely. Company-culture alignment is not directly demonstrated, but the internal training, cross-functional usage, and operational delivery provide some evidence of knowledge sharing and practical ownership.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the TECHNICAL SKILLS section, replace "Platforms and tools: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker, dbt, dbt Cloud scheduler, Streamlit, Docker, pytest, R Markdown" with a more ATS-explicit grouping such as: "Cloud and data platforms: GCP (BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench), Looker" and "Orchestration, deployment and quality: dbt, dbt Cloud scheduler, scheduled notebooks, Docker, pytest, Streamlit." This uses only technologies already supported by the document while making the GCP and orchestration experience easier to identify.

2. In the PROFESSIONAL PROFILE, change "Data Scientist with experience building and evaluating forecasting, churn-modelling and experimentation solutions using Python, SQL and cloud data tools" to "Data Scientist with 4+ years of experience building and evaluating forecasting, churn-modelling and experimentation solutions using Python, SQL and GCP data tools." Keep the rest of the profile truthful, and retain the explicit distinction that the forecasting workflow uses scheduled notebooks and the churn workflow uses batch scoring rather than claiming API deployment.

3. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the forecasting bullet to make the production workflow and data handoff more ATS-readable: "Built and scheduled a weekly LightGBM forecasting workflow in GCP Vertex AI Workbench, engineering calendar, price and menu-position features and writing six-week recipe-and-region forecasts to BigQuery for operational reporting in Looker." Retain the existing WAPE and food-waste results in a following sentence or bullet.

4. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the churn bullet to explicitly surface the existing pipeline terminology: "Developed a weekly XGBoost churn batch-scoring pipeline in BigQuery using dbt and dbt Cloud scheduling; engineered customer features and supported retention targeting of top-decile customers." Keep the existing 10% holdout result. Do not describe this as real-time serving or API deployment.

5. In the Thistlebox experience section, clarify the scope of deployment ownership in the Streamlit bullet while preserving the useful Docker keyword: "Built and containerised a Streamlit calculator for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests; wrote the Dockerfile, and the data platform team deployed it to Cloud Run. Used by approximately 25 people in product and growth." This is more precise about the candidate's contribution and avoids any implication that the candidate personally operated the deployment.

6. In the PROFESSIONAL PROFILE or immediately after the technical skills list, add one concise line that accurately frames the engineering transition: "Production-oriented practices: scheduled batch workflows, Docker-based packaging, pytest unit testing, and data delivery to BigQuery; currently transitioning from applied data science toward machine learning engineering." This consolidates relevant evidence already present without implying experience with model APIs, monitoring, or MLOps platforms not documented.
